sentences.text:
M/S Shubham Industries vs State Of U.P. And Others on 7
February, 2020

Author: Sudhir Agarwal
Bench: Sudhir Agarwal
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Court No. - 34
Case :- Application U/S 482 No. - 7635 of 2005
Applicant :- M/S Shubham Industries

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P. and Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Syed Ali Murtaza

Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.
Heard Sri Vimlendu Tripathi, Advocate, holding brief of Sri S.A. Murtaza, Advocate, for applicant and learned A.G.A. for State.

2. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed praying for quashing of proceedings in Criminal Complaint Case No. 778 of 1998, under Sections 7(V), 16(I)(a)(II) of prevention of Food Adulteration Act read with Rule 32(e)(f) of Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, pending in the Court of 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Basti.
3. It is contended that no sanction has been obtained but it is a question of fact which objection, if taken by applicant, can be examined by Court below.

So far as allegation levelled against applicant are concerned, after going through the complaint and others documents, I am of the view that at this stage it cannot be said that commission of cognizable offence is not made out or there is any error M/S Shubham Industries vs State Of U.P. And Others on 7 February, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152396161/
1 legal or otherwise in the order passed by Court below against applicants.

entities.text: Shubham Industries vs State Of U.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The allegations being factual in nature can be decided only subject to evidence.
In view of settled legal proposition, no findings can be recorded about veracity of allegations at this juncture in absence of evidence.
Apex Court has highlighted that jurisdiction under Section 482 Cr.P.C. be sparingly/rarely invoked with complete circumspection and caution.

Recently in Md. Allauddin Khan Vs. The State of Bihar and others (2019) 6 SCC 107, Supreme Court observed as to what should be examined by High Court in an application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. and in paras 15, 16 and 17 said as under :
?15.

entities.text: Md. Allauddin Khan Vs. The State of Bihar and others (2019) 6 SCC 107
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The High Court should have seen that when a specific grievance of the appellant in his complaint was that respondent Nos. 2 and 3 have committed the offences punishable under Sections 323, 379 read with Section 34 IPC, then the question to be examined is as to whether there are allegations of commission of these two offences in the complaint or not.
In other words, in order to see whether any prima facie case against the accused for taking its cognizable is made out or not, the Court is only required to see the allegations made in the complaint.
In the absence of any finding recorded by the High Court on this material question, the impugned order is legally unsustainable.
16. The second error is that the High Court in para 6 held that there are contradictions in the statements of the witnesses on the point of occurrence.

17. In our view, the High Court had no jurisdiction to appreciate the evidence of the proceedings under Section 482 of the Code Of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (for short ?Cr.P.C.?) because whether there are contradictions or/and inconsistencies in the statements of the witnesses is essentially an issue relating to appreciation of evidence and the same can be gone into by the Judicial Magistrate during trial when the entire evidence is adduced by the parties.
That stage is yet to come in this case.?
(emphasis added)

4. Very recently, Apex Court in Criminal Appeal No. 1817 of 2019 (M. Jayanthi Vs. K.R. Meenakshi and another) decided on 02.12.2019 has held:
?It is too late in the day to seek reference to any authority for the proposition that while invoking the power underSection 482 Cr.P.C for quashing a complaint or a charge, the Court should not embark upon an enquiry into the validity of the evidence available.

entities.text: Criminal Appeal No. 1817 of 2019 (M. Jayanthi Vs. K.R. Meenakshi and another)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: All that the Court should see is as to whether there are allegations in the complaint which form the basis for the ingredients that constitute certain offences complained of.

The Court may also be entitled to see (i) whether the preconditions requisite for taking cognizance have been complied with or not; and (ii) whether the allegations contained in the complaint, even if accepted in entirety, would not constitute the offence alleged.?
5. No material irregularity in the procedure followed by Court below has been pointed out.
It is not a case of grave injustice justifying interference in this application at this stage.

2 6.

entities.text: Shubham Industries vs State Of U.P. And Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The application lacks merit and is accordingly dismissed.
